question: Which of the following Articles of Indian Constitution provides Right against Exploitation? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Article 19
Article 23
Article 21
Article 14
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 23

Explanation:
The Right against Exploitation is enshrined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution. Article 23 prohibits trafficking in human beings, beggar (forced labor without payment), and child labor. It is a fundamental right. Article 19 provides the Right to Freedom, Article 21 the Right to Life, and Article 14 the Right to Equality. The Right against Exploitation protects vulnerable sections of society from various forms of exploitation.

☛ What does Article 23 prohibit? → Human trafficking and forced labor
☛ Which article prohibits child labor? → Article 24
☛ Which article provides the Right to Equality? → Article 14
☛ Which article provides the Right to Life? → Article 21

question: Which section of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) empowers an executive magistrate to prohibit an assembly of more than four persons in an area? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Section 231
Section 111
Section 144
Section 357
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Section 144

Explanation:
Section 144 of the CrPC empowers an executive magistrate to prohibit an assembly of more than four persons in a particular area. This section is used to prevent imminent danger or disturbance, such as riots, epidemics, or threats to public order. The magistrate can issue an order that remains in force for a maximum of two months, but the state government can extend it up to six months. This is a preventive measure aimed at maintaining law and order. Section 231 is unrelated to criminal procedure. Section 111 deals with inquiry after conviction, and Section 357 deals with compensation to victims.

☛ How long can the state government extend Section 144 order? → 6 months
☛ What type of section is Section 144? → Preventive section
☛ What does Section 357 of CrPC deal with? → Compensation to victim

question: The Constitution of India came into force in: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1948
1950
1947
1949
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1950

Explanation:
The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, but it came into force with full effect on 26 January 1950. This day is celebrated as Republic Day in India. With the enforcement of the Constitution, India became a sovereign, democratic republic. The Constitution replaced the Government of India Act 1935. The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to draft it. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

question: Which of the following acts in India was based on report of a committee headed by the British Prime Minister Lord North? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Charter's Act 1793
Pitts India Act 1784
Government of India act 1858
Regulating Act 1773
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Regulating Act 1773

Explanation:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was based on the report of a committee headed by the British Prime Minister Lord North. This Act marked the first direct involvement of the British government in controlling the affairs of the East India Company. It created the position of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings becoming the first to hold the office. The Act also established a Supreme Court in Calcutta. Its main objective was to bring transparency and accountability to the Company's administration. This Act was a significant step towards administrative reforms in British India. It aimed to regulate the Company's political and administrative functions, thereby laying the foundation for future governance acts.

question: A parliamentary executive is: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: where the parliament functions as the executive
an executive where there is a parliament
an executive elected by the parliament
an executive who is dependent on the support of the majority in the parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is an executive who is dependent on the support of the majority in the parliament

Explanation:
A parliamentary executive is a system in which the executive (council of ministers) depends on the support of the majority in the lower house of parliament for its existence and tenure. This system is based on the Westminster model, followed in countries like India, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia. In this system, the President or Monarch is the nominal head, while the Prime Minister is the real executive head. The council of ministers is collectively responsible to the parliament. If the government loses a confidence vote, it must resign or call for new elections. This arrangement ensures the stability and accountability of the government.

☛ From which country did India adopt the parliamentary system? → United Kingdom
☛ To whom is the council of ministers responsible? → Parliament
☛ What type of head is the President considered? → Nominal head
☛ What happens if the government loses a confidence vote? → Resignation or new elections

Explanation:

question: The first election for the provincial legislatures in British India was held in the year: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)

question: How  many fundamental rights were enshrined in the Constitution of India of 1950? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Five
Seven
Eight
Six
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seven

Explanation:
When the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950, it originally enshrined seven fundamental rights under Articles 12 to 35. These included Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32), and Right to Property (Article 31). Later, the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of fundamental rights, making it a legal right under Article 300A. Hence, currently there are six fundamental rights.

question: The Central Government is bound to present the 'Annual Financial Report/Statement' as per ________ of the Constitution of India. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)

question: A civil servant is NOT allowed to become which of the following? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)

Member of Parliament

Explanation:
In India, civil servants (e.g., IAS, IPS officers) are required to maintain political neutrality under the Constitution and service rules. This restriction applies during their service tenure, while after retirement they can join politics. question: What is the maximum time gap between two successive sessions of the Parliament? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: 6 months
3 months
8 months
1 year
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 months

Explanation:
The maximum gap between two successive sessions of the Indian Parliament is six months, as per Article 85 of the Constitution. This constitutional requirement ensures that Parliament meets at least twice a year, and the interval between sessions does not exceed six months. This provision maintains continuity and accountability in democratic governance. There are three sessions of Parliament: Budget Session (February-May), Monsoon Session (July-September), and Winter Session (November-December). This rule is derived from the British parliamentary tradition.

The 61st Amendment (1988) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years for Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. question: Who was the first President of Constituent Assembly of independent India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/03/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:
The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in 1946. Its first meeting was held on 9 December 1946, in which Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the temporary chairman (pro tem speaker). However, on 11 December 1946, Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly. Hence, Dr Rajendra Prasad was the first President of the Constituent Assembly of independent India. He later became the first President of India. Dr B.R. question: An introductory statement in a constitution that states the reasons and guiding values of the constitution is called: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Preamble
Clause
Fundamental rights
Article
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Preamble

Explanation:
The Preamble is an introductory statement in a constitution that outlines the reasons, purposes, and guiding values behind the constitution. It acts as a key to understanding the framers' intent and the fundamental principles of the nation. The Indian Constitution's Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India' and declares justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as core values. It is often called the soul of the constitution. The Preamble was amended in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment, adding the words 'socialist, secular, and integrity'. It is an integral part of the constitution and aids in judicial interpretation. The Preamble reflects the philosophy and basic structure of the constitution.

☛ How many ideals are mentioned in the Preamble? → Four: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
☛ Which amendment amended the Preamble? → The 42nd Amendment (1976).
☛ From which constitution was the Preamble borrowed? → The US Constitution.
☛ Is the Preamble enforceable by courts? → Yes, the Supreme Court held it as part of the constitution and enforceable.
question_hi: संविधान में वह परिचयात्मक कथन जिसमें संविधान के कारणों और मार्गदर्शक मूल्यों का उल्लेख किया जाता है, कहलाता है: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/03/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following is NOT a source of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Constitution of Ireland
Constitution of France
Constitution of Denmark
Constitution of U.S.A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constitution of Denmark

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution has borrowed many features from various constitutions. The Constitution of Ireland inspired the Directive Principles of State Policy. The Constitution of France provided the ideals of Republic and Liberty, Equality, Fraternity. The U.S. Constitution contributed Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review, and the impeachment of the President. However, the Constitution of Denmark is not a source of the Indian Constitution. India also drew from Britain, Canada, Australia, the Soviet Union, and South Africa, but Denmark had no direct influence. Hence, the Constitution of Denmark is not a source.

question: In the absence of the President of India, who would take charge of the President's office?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha
Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister
Senior most judge of the Supreme Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 65 of the Indian Constitution, in the absence of the President, the Vice-President discharges the functions of the President. The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha. If the President's office falls vacant due to death, resignation, or impeachment, the Vice-President can act as President for a maximum of six months, during which a new President is elected. The Chief Justice of India or Prime Minister does not have this power. Only the Vice-President assumes the President's duties in his absence.

question: Article 21A was added to the Constitution of India by which constitutional amendment act?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 94th Constitutional Amendment
42nd Constitutional Amendment
86th Constitutional Amendment
93rd Constitutional Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 86th Constitutional Amendment

Explanation:
Article 21A was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. This article provides the right to free and compulsory education for all children between the ages of 6 and 14 years. It transformed education from a Directive Principle into a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution. Along with this, Article 45 was amended to reflect the state's responsibility for early childhood care. The 86th Amendment was a landmark step to ensure every child's right to education, later enforced by the RTE Act, 2009. This amendment marked a significant shift in India's educational policy.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head to aid and advice the president, who shall exercise his/her functions in accordance to the advice? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Article 79(1)
Article 74(1)
Article 72(1)
Article 73(1)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 74(1)

Explanation:
Article 74(1) of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head to aid and advise the President, who shall exercise his/her functions in accordance with the advice. This Article is the cornerstone of the parliamentary system of government, where the President is the formal head and real power lies with the Council of Ministers. The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) clarified that the President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers. Article 74(1) defines the structure and functioning of the Council of Ministers, while Article 75 deals with the appointment and responsibility of the Prime Minister and other ministers.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद यह प्रावधान करता है कि राष्ट्रपति की सहायता और सलाह के लिए प्रधानमंत्री के नेतृत्व में मंत्रिपरिषद होगी, जो राष्ट्रपति द्वारा सलाह के अनुसार अपने कार्य करेगा? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a 'fundamental right' in the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Right to Freedom
Cultural and Educational Right
Right to Speech
Right to Equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Speech

Explanation:
The list of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution includes Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), and Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30). The 'Right to Speech' is not a separate Fundamental Right; it is part of the Right to Freedom under Article 19(1)(a). Article 19 guarantees six freedoms: speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession. Thus, the right to speech is a component, not an independent Fundamental Right.

question: Which country's constitution has been considered by India for the 'Principles of Liberty, Equality & Fraternity'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: France
Britain
Australia
Ireland
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is France

Explanation:
The principles of 'Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity' enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution are inspired by the French Constitution. These ideals originated from the French Revolution (1789) with the motto 'Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité'. The Indian Constituent Assembly adopted these principles between 1947-49. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar emphasized their importance for Indian society in the Assembly. Apart from France, India borrowed the parliamentary system from Britain, Directive Principles of State Policy from Ireland, and the concurrent list from Australia. The Preamble of India declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic, ensuring liberty, equality, and fraternity for all citizens.

☛ Year of French Revolution → 1789

☛ Article for 'Equality' in Indian Constitution → Article 14
